That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: Two of the three symptoms are internal funnel decay (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and only one is competitive. Onboarding is the upstream constraint: memory_86 ties shortened onboarding to completion and time-to-value across self-serve, and memory_31 ties signup simplification to a durable first-week activation lift. That makes simplify_onboarding the single lever that plausibly moves both declining metrics at once, and its gains are structural rather than purchased. Promotional pricing (memory_73) buys volume in exactly the segment the competitor is targeting, but discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are the weakest source of sustainable qualified revenue, and it does nothing for the activation/onboarding decay — a discounted signup that never activates is a churn event with a delay. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the runner-up but treats the symptom downstream of a broken onboarding flow. Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist address neither current decline. I am spending the single verification on memory_73 rather than on my own intended direction because memory_73 is the leadership anchor I am proposing to override, and its weakest point is unexamined: it reports 'acquisition and revenue lift' with no stated horizon, margin effect, or retention follow-up. If the archived record shows the lift was measured over a short window or on gross rather than net revenue, overriding is clearly correct; if it shows durable retained revenue in a price-attack scenario, I should reconsider promotional pricing despite the funnel evidence.
